claim: Demo scope decision (after user question about needing latency groups): 'near' in the shipped mechanism has exactly one coordinate — the latency group (the epic's distance metric, group-binary today, RTT-continuous later). A one-group cluster has a uniformly-zero affinity gradient, so the smallest honest code-near-data demo is two operator-pinned ZONES on one host: data loads while only zone-a nodes exist (zone-local by construction), the service converges into zone-a. Node-level within-zone affinity = the epic's recorded RTT-later extension, not demo scope.

Two half-built production mechanisms FINISHED (not bypassed) for the demo: (1) native_js handler map — NativeJsDriver required context.handlerMap but nothing in production assembled one (even pgwire-runtime-module was imported by nothing); ServiceRuntimeLifecycle now owns a registry (registerNativeJsHandler) supplied to driver.prepare when the caller passes none, and createRuntimeStartupWiring registers pgwire + the new generic sql-query-loop module; (2) zone pinning — latency.pinnedGroupId config (LATENCY_GROUP_ID env) honored INSIDE the LatencyGroupManager's assignment decision, keeping it the single owner of nodes.latency_group_id (RTT never consulted under a pin).

Live run 1 surfaced a PRE-EXISTING join-path wart (not introduced here, demo made robust against it): after a replica_operations-p1 leadership move (node-0 -> node-1 at 06:04:30, CPU pressure from the 100k load), the SEED's join-gate leader-metadata view stayed stale 30+s ('Bootstrap blocked - missing raft group leaders' while node-1 demonstrably held leadership), and joiners exhaust their impatient retry budget (4 attempts/resume, dead in ~26s) and EXIT — a healthy cluster permanently rejects joiners that nothing restarts. Demo fix = orchestrator-style supervision (respawn exited joiners, max 5). Follow-up quest candidate: join-gate leader metadata freshness vs joiner retry budget mismatch.

Live run 2 surfaced and FIXED a real product bug: a runtime service created AFTER boot could NEVER be placed — RuntimeServiceRebalancerOwner.refresh() (whose own doc says 'safe to call on every service_definitions change') was only invoked from setLeader(true), so post-boot createService rows sat unowned until a service_definitions-p1 leadership move. Fixed by finishing the intended wiring: the owner subscribes to systemTableCache.onCacheChange and refreshes on service_definitions changes (no-op while not leader; unsubscribed on shutdown); pinned in test/bootstrap/runtime-service-rebalancer-owner.test.js (deploy-after-attach case). Built-ins masked this because they register before leadership attach.

Live run 3 surfaced and FIXED a cluster-wide product wart: ALL THREE built-in meta services (sys-wasm-meta, sys-admin-meta, sys-postgres-wire) shipped status=active replica_count=3, but their command handling runs IN-PROCESS via the meta router — no lifecycle module exists for their runtime_refs — so every cluster permanently churned doomed failed-ADD retry loops (timeline-proven: the built-ins' executing ADDs held the concurrent-ADD budget at 06:25, the demo service's ADDs all skipped budget_exceeded at 06:26:40). Fixed: all three ship replica_count 0 (the documented ship-not-started mechanism); pgwire's not-started posture is now explicit rather than emergent from the handler-map bug (with the map wired, replica 3 would have bound :5432 on every placed node — verifier catch). Likely also removes standing rebalance-churn noise from every cluster boot.

USER DIRECTIVE + product problem (runs 4-5): an internal pacing problem must not rely on client fidelity — the 100k-row load had batches fail to the CLIENT with 'Distributed operation failed due to participant failures' (participant query timeouts ~1000ms) while the cluster was digesting its own control-plane settling (sql_transaction_participants replica creates, leadership moves). Per ARCH-0016/ARCH-0017 this is a write-path backpressure violation: the ingress pressure governor should DEFER with retry-after, or the distributed write coordinator should absorb transient participant timeouts within a derived budget, before exporting failure. The loader batch-retry added to the demo is client-side belt-and-braces only, NOT the product answer. Follow-up quest candidate: write-path internal pacing under formation-adjacent load (participant timeout budgets + governor engagement for writes).

Live run 7 peeled the next layer: replica svc-movielens-topn-r1 CREATED AND COMPLETED on node 74a0d84d (adapter camelCase/snake_case validation fix worked) — but it is INVISIBLE: ServiceRuntimeLifecycle._stateProjectionWriter (the designed services-table projection of runtime replica state) has ZERO production callers (setStateProjectionWriter wired nowhere), so placed replicas never appear in the services table — the rebalancer's currentReplicas view stays empty (it keeps re-planning ADDs), observers see replicas=0, and attribution cannot be confirmed. FOURTH half-wired mechanism on this single path (handler map, owner refresh-on-change, descriptor field contract, state projection). Fix = follow-on quest runtime-replica-state-projection; demo quest stops short of SOLVED until then (explicit TEST-0033 split).

Live run 9 diagnosis (post-projection): service ADDs again budget_exceeded because ship-not-started was DEFEATED BY TWO CLAMPS — getPolicyTargetReplicaCount's '||' coerced explicit 0 to the default 1, and validateReplicaCount's Math.max(min,...) clamped any surviving 0 up — directly contradicting getRuntimeServicePolicy's documented 'an explicit 0 is honored (place none)'. The resurrected meta-service replicas (pgwire even placed, binding :5432 — the verifier's warning realized) held the ordinary concurrent-ADD lane (limit 4 = 5 minus 1 reserved priority slot) every cycle. Both clamps fixed with RUNTIME_SERVICE target-0 passthrough, planner-level guard test added. SEPARATE pre-existing wart observed: sql_transactions-p1 add-storm (313 planned/310 blocked target_node_already_occupied in 10min) churning the priority lane — quest candidate, ledger lookup pending.

Live run 10 (staleness detector fired at 210s as designed — user directive validated) peeled TWO more attach-time-only defects, both FIXED+pinned: (1) the runtime-service owner's leadership sink resolved the service_definitions-p1 partition service ONCE at composition — 4/5 nodes logged 'partition service not found; owner will not be leadership-gated (inert)' because only the seed hosted a replica then, so the FIRST leadership move off the seed left the cluster with NO runtime-service planner; fixed with level-triggered retry wiring (unref'd 5s interval until the local replica exists). (2) ship-not-started had a THIRD clamp: isCriticalState/getCriticalReason floor at minReplicaCount regardless of an explicit target 0, forcing 'replica_count_below_minimum' adds for the built-ins; fixed with min = Math.min(min, target). Total intent/code mismatches found by this demo campaign: seven.

Run 13 (single-zone) root-caused a cluster-wide FREEZE, full forensics from the persisted SQLite + logs: two formation REPLACEs moved replica_operations-p1 off node a66a2b10 (completed 09:16:52, 09:17:13); from 09:17:12 writers hit 'No handler registered for partition service replica_operations-p1' (query-executor, node c82d6f41) and the ops table received ZERO writes for the remaining ~5min — freezing 5 in-flight REPLACE ops (pinning the entire maxConcurrentAdds=5 budget: run 12's budget_exceeded root), freezing membership reconcile ('not the control_plane_publications writer' spam — control_plane_publications-p1 was itself mid-REPLACE among the frozen 5), and failing the loader. The designed recovery EXISTS (handleNoHandlerCandidate -> markTemporarilyUnroutable -> maybeAwaitRuntimeRoutingRepair with forceAuthoritativeRefresh, query-executor-write-retry-routing.js:219-249) but did not restore routing within 5 minutes — suspected mutual dependency: repairing replica_operations-p1 routing needs fresh control-plane state whose publication was blocked on the frozen ops. Formation-vs-steady-state circular class, live-evidenced.

RUN-24 (post leader-durability-fitness 9234e904 + zombie-lifecycle d0f7f776): the run-23 silent-freeze class is GONE — no wedge, no silence; the failure is LOUD and immediate, which is the fitness/heal pair working as designed at the boundary. NEW HEAD CLASS: the demo dies at its FIRST CREATE TABLE ~6s after formation (11:15:55, formation 6.4s) with 'Unable to satisfy minimum routable provisioning cohort required=2 provisionable=0' — all three target nodes deferred with operation_ledger_self_move_in_flight because the run-20 ledger self-move hold was legitimately engaged (ledger replicas spreading off the seed at 11:15:29-33 during boot). The reason IS already classified transient in TRANSIENT_PROVISIONING_SHORTFALL_REASONS (run-22 work) but transient classification only lowers the fallback minimum — with provisionable=0 it fail-fasts to the CLIENT, violating internal-pacing-not-client-fidelity. This is exactly the run-22 recorded follow-up (full-hold fail-fast) now binding live. Cosmetic co-find: the interlock blocking message embeds the ADMITTED operation's partitionId (the user table) in a message claiming 'Operation-ledger partition X self-move in flight' (rebalance-coordinator-ledger-interlock-admission.js:407-425) — mislabeled, confused forensics. Successor quest authored: provisioning-admission-ledger-hold-transient-wait (P1). Trajectory: run-19/20 = 0 completions (formation wedges), run-22 = 3, run-23 = 19 (ledger froze mid-run), run-24 = 0 loads but FAST-LOUD at a well-understood transient boundary — each retired class stays retired (no recurrence of interlock wedge, quorum starvation, ghost rows, or the zombie freeze in run-24 logs).
